newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine needs more than budget for IMF credit - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine needs more than budget for IMF credit - IMF.

text.p: Ukraine must do much more than pass its much-delayed budget to qualify for a multi-billion dollar credit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the fund's senior resident representative in Kiev said on Friday.
Ukraine is required to meet 41 conditions, including approval of the 1997 budget, before it can receive a $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) from the international funding body.

"The purpose of the EFF is to support programmes with strong content in terms of structural reforms. Therefore we do not consider adoption of the 1997 budget as a sufficient step to justify the EFF," Patrick Lenain told Reuters.
Lenain said Ukraine has met only some of the conditions to receive the EFF, to succeed a $867 million stand-by credit which expired in February.
"In order to obtain financial support from the IMF, Ukraine also needs to take measures to deregulate the private sector, reform the tax system and to strengthen its banks," Lenain said.

Latest predictions by Ukrainian parliamentary deputies put passage of the budget by the end of this month, after the government -- which has been working on revisions since last December -- hands it to parliament for final debate.
Parliament and the government also must pass seven of nine tax reform laws to underpin the budget and overhaul Ukraine's unwieldy and punitive tax system.
Ukraine has also proposed laws to reduce the number of licences necessary to operate a business from about 90 to 30.

The budget, which under Ukrainian law should have been passed by January 1, forecasts gross domestic product of 100.4 billion hryvnias ($54.6 billion), a deficit of 5.7 percent of GDP, and inflation of 24.9 percent against 39.7 percent in 1996.
